vocabulary.SELF-ONLY: the caller may act only on its own subject
vocabulary.FOREIGN-READ: a foreign subject may be read, widened only by literal fleet.observe
vocabulary.FOREIGN-WRITE: a foreign subject may be written, widened only by literal fleet.admin
vocabulary.ADDRESSED: the argument names a recipient; the sender is bound by the resolver
vocabulary.ATTRIBUTION: the argument is stored as a label and selects nothing
vocabulary.NOT-IDENTITY: regex hit that is not a caller argument, with the reason
vocabulary.ESCALATE: disposition not readable from the code; evidence and a recommendation given, ISO and VECTOR decide

sites.evidence: Written to the analytics event as a label; it selects no document. So the label is caller-controlled and must not be read as identity.

sites.binding_today: none; session_id is stored on the clu report as a label (L-D9 option 2: ATTRIBUTION, no code)

sites.binding_today: isTaskOwner (dispatch/shared.ts): claimedBy equals credentialPrincipal, or claimedBy "dispatcher" and sessionId equals the principal. sessionId is attribution; a missing sessionId never matches. claimedBy is written from credentialPrincipal only (RD-5 PR-K, plan 19.1).
sites.evidence: args.sessionId is stored on the claim (claims.ts:97 (single claim at :96, batch at :311)) and compared by later calls: claims.ts:76 treats an equal sessionId as an idempotent re-claim and returns the task data to a different program, and completion.ts:537, completion.ts:870 and claims.ts:190 accept data.sessionId === auth.programId as ownership. A caller-chosen value therefore enters two authorization comparisons.
sites.recommendation: Remove sessionId from every authorization comparison; claimedBy is the owner. Label sessionId ATTRIBUTION after that.
